c0.title: Forklift and Pedestrian Traffic Signs
c0.descriptionHtml: Signs for forklift and pedestrian traffic: forklift lanes, crossings, blind corners, pedestrian walkways, battery charging and propane cylinder change areas, docks and rack aisles. An operator often cannot see a person standing close to the load, so the warning has to reach the people on foot first.

seo.title: Forklift Safety Signs | Forklift Traffic, Pedestrian Crossing | CGAP
seo.description: Forklift traffic, pedestrian crossing, battery charging and propane change signs for warehouses, plants and docks. 8x12 aluminum, made in USA.

metafields.value:
Where to post

  • At aisle entrances where forklifts and people share the floor.
  • At crossings by doors, break rooms, restrooms and time clocks, on both sides of the crossing.
  • At blind corners and rack ends, next to a convex mirror.
  • At battery charging and propane cylinder change areas.
  • At dock doors and dock plates.

Standards to know

OSHA 1910.178 covers powered industrial trucks: operator training, safe operation, and the charging and refueling areas, where smoking is prohibited. OSHA 1910.176 says permanent aisles and passageways used by mechanical handling equipment must be appropriately marked. Signs work together with floor marking, mirrors and a written traffic plan.

Signing a whole site?

Our kits put every sign one area needs in a single order, priced below buying the same signs one at a time.

  • Forklift traffic zone kit, 8 signs
  • Forklift battery charging area kit, 8 signs
  • Warehouse sign kits

Common questions

Where should a pedestrian crossing sign go?

On both sides of the crossing facing people on foot, plus a sign facing the forklift lane so operators expect people there.

Can you add our speed limit or lane rules?

Yes. Custom signs are priced close to catalog signs.

c1.title: Pinch Point Signs
c1.descriptionHtml: Pinch point and nip point warnings for conveyors, rollers, gears, chains, doors, hatches, lift gates and hinged covers. Most are small, specific CAUTION signs placed right at the spot where fingers and hands get caught.

seo.title: Pinch Point Signs | Nip Point and Crush Hazard Warnings | CGAP
seo.description: Pinch point and nip point warning signs for conveyors, rollers, doors, hatches and lift gates. 8x12 rust-resistant aluminum, made in USA.

metafields.value:
Where to post

  • Belt and roller nips, chain and sprocket drives.
  • Closing doors, gates, hatches and hinged lids.
  • Scissor lifts, dock levelers and lift tables.
  • Clamps, fixtures and presses where hands load parts.

Put the sign where someone sees it from the spot where they would reach in.

Signs and guards

OSHA 1910.212 requires guarding for hazards such as in-running nip points and rotating parts. A sign does not replace a guard. It marks the hazards that remain, like a door edge or a hatch lid, and reminds people not to reach past a guard.

Signing a whole site?

Our kits put every sign one area needs in a single order, priced below buying the same signs one at a time.

  • Conveyor system kit, 8 signs
  • Conveyor and sortation kit, 8 signs
  • Manufacturing plant sign kits

Common questions

CAUTION or WARNING?

CAUTION fits minor to moderate injury such as pinched fingers. Use WARNING or DANGER where the point can crush or amputate.

Do you have a conveyor kit?

Yes. The conveyor kits cover drives, nips, crossovers and emergency stops.

c2.title: Hot Work and Welding Signs
c2.descriptionHtml: Signs for welding, cutting, brazing and other hot work: hot work permit areas, fire watch, welding screens and curtains, oxy-fuel cylinders and the places where sparks can reach combustibles.

seo.title: Hot Work and Welding Signs | Hot Work Permit, Fire Watch | CGAP
seo.description: Hot work permit, fire watch, welding area and oxy-fuel cylinder signs for shops, plants and job sites. 8x12 aluminum, made in USA.

metafields.value:
Where to post

  • Welding bays, booths and screens.
  • Areas where hot work needs a permit, and areas where it is not allowed.
  • Near combustibles, dust or flammable vapor.
  • Fire watch stations and extinguisher points.
  • Oxy-fuel cylinder storage and carts.

Standards to know

OSHA 1910.252 covers fire prevention for welding and cutting, including inspecting the area and authorizing the work, preferably with a written permit, and a fire watch that in many cases stays at least half an hour after the work ends. NFPA 51B is the common reference for hot work permit programs. Construction work falls under 29 CFR 1926 Subpart J.
